'''Peter Reed Saulson''' (born October 30, 1954) is an American physicist and professor at [[Syracuse University]]. He is best known as a former spokesperson for the [[LIGO Scientific Collaboration|LIGO collaboration]] serving from 2003 to 2007 and research on [[gravitational wave detector]]s.<ref>{{cite web |title=Peter R. Saulson |url=https://thecollege.syr.edu/people/faculty/saulson-peter-r/ |publisher=College of Arts & Sciences at Syracuse University |access-date=2 May 2021 |language=en-us}}</ref><ref name="ligo-nas"/><ref name="life's work"/>

==Education==
Saulson was born October 30, 1954, in [[Baltimore]], [[Maryland]], into a [[Jew]]ish family.<ref name="life's work">{{cite news |last1=O'Brien |first1=John |title=Einstein discovery an emotional payoff for SU researcher |url=https://www.syracuse.com/su-news/2016/02/einstein_syracuse_university_g.html |access-date=2 May 2021 |work=[[Syracuse Post-Standard]] |date=15 February 2016 |language=en}}</ref> studied physics at [[Harvard University]] where he earned a bachelor's degree  ([[Latin honors#United States|magna cum laude]]) in 1976. He later studied at [[Princeton University]] where he received a master's degree in 1978 and a doctorate in 1981. He was then a post-doctoral scholar at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], where he started in 1985 and worked as principal research scientist until 1989. In 1989 he was a visiting scientist at the [[Joint Institute for Laboratory Astrophysics]] in [[Boulder, Colorado]].

==Career==
Saulson is [[Martin A. Pomerantz]] '37 Professor of Physics at [[Syracuse University]] where he co-leads the Gravitational-Wave Astronomy Group.<ref name="SU NAS">{{cite news |last1=Enslin |first1=Rob |title=Physicist to be Recognized by National Academy of Sciences |url=https://news.syr.edu/blog/2017/01/26/physicist-to-be-recognized-by-national-academy-of-sciences/ |access-date=2 May 2021 |work=SU News |date=January 26, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Holmes |first1=Judy |title=SU alumnus and family endow physics professorship, graduate fellowship |url=https://news.syr.edu/blog/2008/02/07/su-alumnus-and-family-endow-physics-professorship-graduate-fellowship/ |access-date=2 May 2021 |work=SU News |date=February 7, 2008}}</ref> He was associate professor there from 1991 to 1999 and head of the physics department from 2010 to 2013.<ref name="SU scholar 03"/> In 2000–01, he was a visiting professor at [[Louisiana State University]] and in 2000 Interferometer Commissioning Leader at [[LIGO]] and [[Caltech]].

Saulson was the first elected speaker of the [[LIGO Scientific Collaboration]], succeeding LIGO co-founder [[Rainer Weiss]].<ref name="ligo-nas"/>

==Awards and honors==
Saulson was named a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2003 for "his contributions to experimental gravitational physics including pioneering studies of thermal mechanisms affecting interferometer performance and for his educational contributions including authoring one of the most influential books in the field."<ref>{{cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2003&unit_id=DGRAV&institution=Syracuse%20University |website=www.aps.org |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |access-date=2 May 2021 |language=en}}</ref> He was named Syracuse University's 2003-04 University Scholar/Teacher of the Year.<ref name="SU scholar 03">{{cite news |last1=Byrnes |first1=Edward |title=Peter R. Saulson honored as Syracuse University's 2003-04 University Scholar/Teacher of the Year |url=https://news.syr.edu/blog/2003/10/09/peter-r-saulson-honored-as-syracuse-universitys-2003-04-university-scholarteacher-of-the-year/ |access-date=2 May 2021 |work=SU News |date=October 9, 2003}}</ref>

In 2016 he received the [[National Academy of Sciences]] Award for Scientific Discovery with [[Gabriela González]], his former PhD student, and [[David Reitze]].<ref name="ligo-nas">{{cite news |last1=Clavin |first1=Whitney |title=National Academy of Sciences Honors LIGO Researchers |url=https://www.ligo.caltech.edu/WA/news/ligo20170126 |access-date=2 May 2021 |work=LIGO Lab: Caltech |date=January 26, 2017}}</ref><ref name="SU NAS"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Gabriela González, David Reitze, and Peter Saulson |url=http://www.nasonline.org/programs/awards/2017/Gonzaelz-Reitze-Saulson.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170130211258/http://www.nasonline.org/programs/awards/2017/Gonzaelz-Reitze-Saulson.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 30, 2017 |access-date=2 May 2021 |work=[[National Academy of Sciences]]}}</ref>

In 2026, he was elected to the National Academy of Sciences.<ref>{{cite web|title=National Academy of Sciences Elects Members and International Members - NAS|url=https://www.nasonline.org/news/2026-nas-election/|publisher=National Academy of Sciences|access-date=April 30, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Professor Emeritus of Physics Peter Saulson Elected to the National Academy of Sciences |url=https://news.syr.edu/2026/05/19/professor-emeritus-of-physics-peter-saulson-elected-to-the-national-academy-of-sciences/ |access-date=17 June 2026 |work=[[Syracuse University Today]] |date=19 May 2026}}</ref>
